title: Form Configuration
description: A form widget for collecting user input and storing it in database tables. Use this widget to create data entry interfaces for manual input, configuration settings, user feedback, or any scenario requiring structured data collection. Supports various field types including text, numbers, dropdowns, checkboxes, textareas, datetime pickers, masked secrets and file uploads. Each field maps to a database column, enabling direct data persistence. Can display as a button-triggered modal or inline form.

aiSelection.dataShape: Writes rather than reads. Each formFields[] entry maps one input control to a database column through targetColumn, and submitting stores a row. Field types cover text, number, dropdown, checkbox, textarea, datetime, secret and file, with validation, required flags, defaults and conditional visibility. A file field uploads one file into a FleetFiles namespace of the app and stores the file's key in its string column. A secret field is a masked, write-only input.
useWhen: A person needs to enter or correct data that is then persisted — manual readings, maintenance notes, quality checks, configuration values, feedback.
Input must be structured and validated, with required fields, defaults, or fields that appear only when another field has a given value (conditionalDisplay).
Records should also be deletable or flagged as deleted from the dashboard (deleteButton, deleteFlagColumn).
A record comes with a document, image or data file, such as a new SOP revision as a PDF: a field of type 'file' stores the file with the row (fileNamespace, acceptedFileTypes).
A password or API token is entered: a 'secret' field masks it and never shows the saved value. Target a 'secret: true' column, which FleetDB encrypts.
notFor: Narrowing what other widgets display — that is filtering, not data entry. Use widget-filter-dropdown or widget-filter-calendar.
Sending a command to a device rather than storing a value — use widget-switch, or widget-scada for an industrial symbol with actions.
Showing stored records back to the user — use widget-table.
A single button that only navigates somewhere — use widget-navbutton.

title.title: Title
title.description: The main heading displayed at the top of the form. Use to describe the form's purpose (e.g., 'Add New Device', 'Submit Feedback', 'Configuration Settings').

subTitle.title: Subtitle
subTitle.description: Secondary text displayed below the title. Use for instructions, context, or additional information about the form.

formButton.title: Form Open Button
formButton.description: When enabled, shows a button that opens the form in a modal dialog when clicked. When disabled, the form fields are displayed directly in the widget area. Use button mode for space-constrained layouts or optional data entry.

formButtonStyle.title: Form Open Button Style
formButtonStyle.description: Customization options for the form open button's appearance. Choose a round floating action button with an icon, or a regular button with an icon and a label text, and configure its size, colors and icon to match your application's design. These settings only apply when the Form Open Button is enabled. Every setting except Floating Action Button can be bound to a column, so the button can follow data, for example turning red and reading 'Report fault' while a machine is down.

fab.title: Floating Action Button
fab.description: When enabled (the default, also when unset), the form opens from a round floating action button that shows only the icon. When disabled, it opens from a regular button that shows the icon followed by the Label Text, which says what the form is for at a glance.

label.title: Label Text
label.description: Text on the regular button that opens the form, next to its icon (e.g., 'Report issue', 'Add reading'). Left empty, the button shows only the icon. Only applies when Floating Action Button is disabled. Can be bound to a column; a numeric value is shown as it is.

size.title: Size
size.description: The size of the form open button: small, medium (the default) or large. A floating action button is 40, 56 or 96px; a regular button is 32, 40 or 56px tall. Can be bound to a column holding 'small', 'medium' or 'large'; any other value gives medium.

bgColor.title: Background Color
bgColor.description: The background color of the form open button. Can be set to a specific color value (e.g., '#ff0000' for red) or left as default to use the theme's primary color. Can be bound to a column holding a CSS color; a value that is not a valid color keeps the default.

color.title: Icon and Label Color
color.description: The color of the icon on the form open button, and of the Label Text on a regular button. Can be set to a specific color value (e.g., '#ffffff' for white) or left as default: a floating action button then uses the theme's second chart color, a regular button black or white, whichever reads better on its background. Can be bound to a column holding a CSS color; a value that is not a valid color keeps the default.

iconName.title: Icon Name
iconName.description: Material icon name shown on the form open button. Find icon names at https://fonts.google.com/icons (e.g., 'edit_note', 'build', 'upload_file', 'add_comment'). Leave empty for the default plus sign ('add'). Can be bound to a column holding an icon name, so the icon can reflect a state (e.g., 'warning' while an alarm is active).

formDialogSize.title: Form Dialog Size
formDialogSize.description: Minimum size of the dialog that the Form Open Button opens. By default the dialog is 480px wide (less on small screens) and as tall as its fields, up to 80% of the window height, and it scrolls beyond that. Raise the minimums to give long forms, labels and text areas more room, or to keep the dialog from changing size when conditional fields appear. A minimum never makes the dialog larger than the browser window less 24px on each side, so the dialog and its Submit button always stay on screen. A value that is not a number with an optional unit, such as 'auto', 'calc(100% - 100px)' or a negative number, is ignored with a console warning. These settings only apply when the Form Open Button is enabled.

minWidth.title: Minimum Width
minWidth.description: Minimum dialog width as a number with an optional unit, such as '800px', '60%' or '50vw' (no unit means px; % and vw are a share of the window width). Leave empty for the default. The dialog is normally 480px wide (less on small screens), so only a larger value makes it wider. The fields stay in one column: text fields, dropdowns and text areas widen with the dialog, while number and date fields keep their 200px.

minHeight.title: Minimum Height
minHeight.description: Minimum dialog height as a number with an optional unit, such as '600px', '70%' or '90vh' (no unit means px; % and vh are a share of the window height). Leave empty to fit the dialog to its fields. A short form gets empty space below its last field while the buttons stay at the bottom; set the height of the form's tallest state to keep the dialog from resizing when conditional fields appear. A long form scrolls inside the dialog, and a value above 80% shows more of it at once.

accentColor.title: Highlight Color
accentColor.description: Color of the outline and label of the field being edited, of checked checkboxes and of the Submit button. Leave empty to pick it automatically: the theme's first chart color when it stands out clearly from the form's background (a contrast of at least 3:1), otherwise the form's text color. Set it to match an application's brand color; a chosen color is used as is, so pick one that reads on the background.

deleteButton.title: Show Delete Button
deleteButton.description: When enabled, shows a delete button that allows users to remove existing entries.

deleteFlagColumn.title: Delete-Flag Column
deleteFlagColumn.description: The target table column used to mark records as deleted when the delete button is clicked. This MUST be a boolean column. If the target table has such a deleted_flag column, it should be specified here regardless of the delete button setting.

deleteNavigationRoute.title: Post-Delete Navigation
deleteNavigationRoute.description: The destination path to route to after delete. Use for navigating to a home or main page.

variables.title: Post-Delete Navigation Variables
variables.description: Array of variable definitions for dynamic route segment substitution. Each variable has a label (used in the route string as {{label}}) and a value (the replacement text). Values can be static or bound to data columns for real-time updates.

label.title: Label
label.description: The variable name used in the route string. Reference this in your route using the {{label}} syntax. Use descriptive names like 'temperature', 'status', 'deviceName'.

value.title: Value
value.description: The replacement text that will appear in place of {{label}} in the rendered output. Can be a static value or bound to a data column for dynamic updates.

formFields.title: Form Fields
formFields.description: Array of input fields that make up the form. Each field defines its type, validation rules, and target database column for storage. Fields are rendered in the order specified.

label.title: Label
label.description: The text label displayed next to this form field. Should clearly describe what data the user should enter.

type.title: Field Type
type.description: The input control type: 'dropdown' for selection from predefined options, 'textfield' for single-line text, 'numberfield' for numeric values, 'checkbox' for boolean yes/no, 'textarea' for multi-line text, 'datetime' for date and time selection, 'file' for uploading one file into the app's file storage (FleetFiles), whose key is stored in the target column, 'secret' for a password, token or key that is masked while it is typed (a button shows it). A secret field always starts empty and has no pre-filled value: a saved secret is never shown again. Left empty, it leaves its column out of the save, so a table that keeps the latest row per entity (maintainLatestFlagFor) keeps the stored secret and any other table stores NULL. Point it at a string column declared 'secret: true' in the data template, which FleetDB encrypts and never returns to a board; any other column stores the value as plain text. Required means a new value must be typed on every save, so leave it off in a form that edits existing records.

hiddenField.title: Hidden Field
hiddenField.description: When enabled, this field is hidden from users but its value (typically a default or data-bound value) is still submitted with the form. Useful for including metadata, timestamps, or user IDs automatically.

required.title: Required
required.description: When enabled, users must fill out this field before the form can be submitted. The form will show a validation error if left empty. Ignored when a default value is provided.

description.title: Hint Text
description.description: Helper text displayed below the field to guide users on what to enter. Use for format hints, examples, or clarifying instructions.

targetColumn.title: Target Column
targetColumn.description: The database table and column where this field's value will be stored on form submission. Select from available tables and columns. All fields targeting the same table will be combined into a single row insert.

preFilledValue.title: Pre-filled Value
preFilledValue.description: Pre-filled value for this field when the form loads. Can be a static value or bound to a data source. For a file field, bind it to the target column of the record being edited: the form then shows that file, and a save without a new file keeps it.

preFilledValueMultiline.title: Pre-filled Value
preFilledValueMultiline.description: Pre-filled value for this field when the form loads. Can be a static value or bound to a data source.

preFilledValueBoolean.title: Pre-filled Value
preFilledValueBoolean.description: Pre-filled checked state for this checkbox when the form loads. Can be a static value or bound to a data source.

defaultValue.title: Default Value
defaultValue.description: Default value for this field when the form loads. If the user does not provide a value, this default will be used. Can be a static value or bound to a data source.

defaultValueMultiline.title: Default Value
defaultValueMultiline.description: Default value for this field when the form loads. If the user does not provide a value, this default will be used. Can be a static value or bound to a data source.

defaultValueBoolean.title: Default Value
defaultValueBoolean.description: Default checked state for this checkbox when the form loads. If the user does not change it, this state will be used. Can be a static value or bound to a data source.

min.title: Minimum Value
min.description: The minimum allowed numeric value for numberfield types. Values below this will fail validation.

max.title: Maximum Value
max.description: The maximum allowed numeric value for numberfield types. Values above this will fail validation.

validation.title: Validation Regex
validation.description: A regular expression pattern to validate text input (e.g., '^[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{4}$' for format like 'AB1234'). For a secret field it sets the minimum requirements for a newly typed value, such as '^.{12,}$' for at least 12 characters, '(?=.*[0-9])(?=.*[A-Za-z]).{10,}' for at least 10 characters with a letter and a digit, or '[0-9]{4}' for a 4-digit PIN. The whole value must match. Leave empty to accept any text.

validationMessage.title: Validation Message
validationMessage.description: Shown under the field when the value does not match the Validation Regex, in place of the browser's generic 'Please match the requested format'. Say what is required, such as 'At least 10 characters, with a letter and a digit': a masked secret field gives no other clue. Repeat it in the Hint Text to show it before the user types. Leave empty for the browser's message.

browserPasswordManager.title: Browser Password Manager
browserPasswordManager.description: For a secret field: when enabled, the browser and password manager extensions treat the field as a password, so they may offer to generate a strong one and to save what was typed. Off by default, which suits PINs and short codes: the value is still masked, but nothing offers to save, fill or generate it, and the browser keeps no record of it. Turn it on for real passwords that viewers want their browser to remember.

values.title: Dropdown Values
values.description: The list of selectable options for dropdown field types. Each option has a display label and a stored value.

displayLabel.title: Display Label
displayLabel.description: The text shown to users in the dropdown list.

value.title: Value
value.description: The actual value stored in the database when this option is selected. May differ from the display label.

fileNamespace.title: File Namespace
fileNamespace.description: Required for a file field: the FleetFiles namespace the file is stored in, one of the namespaces in the files section of the data template of the app that owns the target table ('default' when that app declares none). The namespace's accepted content types and maximum object size also apply. The target column (a string column) receives the stored file's key within this namespace.

acceptedFileTypes.title: Accepted File Types
acceptedFileTypes.description: Comma-separated MIME types the field accepts, such as 'application/pdf' or 'image/*, application/pdf'. The file picker offers only these, and the form refuses any other file before uploading it. Keep them within the namespace's content types. Leave empty to accept any file the namespace allows.

maxFileSizeMB.title: Maximum File Size (MB)
maxFileSizeMB.description: Largest file the field accepts, in MB (1 MB = 1,048,576 bytes); the form refuses a larger file before uploading it. Leave empty for the namespace's limit (100 MB unless the data template sets maxObjectBytes). Files up to 6 MB upload everywhere. Larger ones need cloud storage that issues upload links, which an on-premises appliance does not by default, so keep 6 MB or less for a board that runs on an appliance.

fileNameColumn.title: File Name Column
fileNameColumn.description: Optional: a string column, in the same table as the target column, that receives the uploaded file's original name, such as 'Assembly SOP rev C.pdf'. Written only when a new file is uploaded.

fileSizeColumn.title: File Size Column
fileSizeColumn.description: Optional: a numeric (bigint or numeric) column, in the same table as the target column, that receives the uploaded file's size in bytes. Written only when a new file is uploaded.

fileTypeColumn.title: File Type Column
fileTypeColumn.description: Optional: a string column, in the same table as the target column, that receives the uploaded file's content type, such as 'application/pdf'. Written only when a new file is uploaded.

fileUrlColumn.title: File URL Column
fileUrlColumn.description: Optional: a string column, in the same table as the target column, that receives the stored file's permanent platform URL, so that other widgets can show or link the file, such as an embed of a PDF or an image. Opening it needs a signed-in IronFlock session. Written only when a new file is uploaded; it stays empty where the installation serves no file links, and with a Studio version that does not write it.

conditionalDisplay.title: Conditional Display
conditionalDisplay.description: Optionally show this field only when another field in this form currently holds one of a set of values. Leave the controlling field empty to always show this field.

conditionField.title: Conditional On Field
conditionField.description: The Label of another field in this form that controls whether this field is shown. Leave empty to always show this field. The match is against the other field's current value (for dropdowns, the option's stored value).

conditionValues.title: Show If Value In
conditionValues.description: Comma-separated list of values. This field is shown only when the field named in 'Conditional On Field' currently holds one of these values. Example: pump, valve. For a checkbox controller use true or false. Has no effect unless 'Conditional On Field' is set.
